reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Bitcoin Empire as an easy-earning program requiring a 0.1 BTC contribution, paid visa activation, and account qualification. It solicits referrals and presents an 80% compound bonus and other rewards as guaranteed, linking payment and recruitment to promised returns. the available video evidence does not establish that anyone paid, received funds, or that the stated amounts were delivered.

citations.quote: Start from 0.1 BTC and voluntary donation.
you will receive an Entry Level Bonus up to 10th level.
from second direct referrals onward you can get bonus of 80% to all direct referrals under your account.

opening.argument: The presentation uses qualifying language that leaves participation as a choice rather than documenting a compulsory payment: the entry is described as a “voluntary donation,” and the program is presented as an “opportunity” to earn. Those qualifications matter when assessing intent. The available material explains a proposed program, but does not establish that any viewer paid, that any account was activated, or that any reward was actually delivered. A promotional claim about possible income, without proof of a completed transaction or realized loss, is insufficient by itself to characterize the presentation as deceptive.

citations.quote: Start from 0.1 BTC and voluntary donation.
This will give us an opportunity to earn through online accumulation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to the entry amount, visa activation, referrals, and bonus language, but those passages describe proposed program terms, not proof that the speaker deceptively obtained money. “Up to 10th level” is a limit on the described bonus structure, while the evidence still does not establish any payment, payout, or victim. The presentation’s use of “voluntary donation” also undercuts the claim that it depicts a compulsory deposit.

citations.quote: Start from 0.1 BTC and voluntary donation.
you will receive an Entry Level Bonus up to 10th level.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the contribution voluntary does not make the offer non-deceptive when the same presentation ties participation to qualification and activation. More importantly, the slides promise certainty rather than merely describing risk: they say rewards and bonuses are “guaranteed and SURE.” The absence of proof that anyone was paid does not erase the solicitation or the guaranteed-return representation.

citations.quote: To qualify from BTC EMPIRE's donation program
This is use for activation of their account

opening.argument: The material can reasonably be understood as an instructional presentation explaining how a named Bitcoin program is structured. Its title identifies it as a presentation, and the narration walks through entry level, visa activation, referrals, and upgrades step by step. Explaining a system’s stated mechanics is not the same as independently certifying that the system works or guaranteeing an outcome. The diagrams and examples therefore support an educational or operational-demonstration reading: viewers are shown how the program claims to function, while the evidence does not show a completed transaction, actual earnings, or a verified victim.

citations.quote: Bitcoin Empire Tagalog Presentation
Lets start with the Entry Level
Bitcoin Empire offers an upgrade program

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats explanatory mechanics as proof of scam status, but describing entry levels, upgrades, and referral calculations is also consistent with a tutorial about how a program operates. The cited 80% language appears inside that explanation; it does not establish that the presenter verified the figure or that anyone received it. The record shows instruction and diagrams, not a demonstrated fraudulent outcome.

citations.quote: Bitcoin Empire offers an upgrade program
Let's summarise

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not neutral technical education. The instructional steps tell viewers to donate, purchase visas, activate accounts, and recruit direct referrals, while the conclusion urges them to ask partners for the referral link. The presentation also says Bitcoin multiplying is easy and that rewards are guaranteed. Calling solicitation a tutorial does not remove its promotional purpose or its recruitment-based mechanism.

citations.quote: It's just a share share opportunity with Bitcoin Empire.
This is use for activation of their account

opening.argument: The strongest ordinary-commerce reading is that this is a promotion for an external service or affiliate opportunity, not evidence that the creator personally operated a fraudulent scheme. The narration describes a stated program, a small visa charge, and a referral-linked bonus arrangement. But the supplied material does not show a payment being collected, credentials being requested, a withdrawal being refused, or a promised payout failing. Nor does it establish that the speaker controlled the underlying service. A referral promotion may be questionable or unverified without the record proving the defining failure or deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: There is a fee of 0.05 USD per visa.
It's just a share share opportunity with Bitcoin Empire.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a contribution, visa charge, and referral percentages, but those are ordinary features of the advertised service as described; they do not prove that money was taken and not delivered. The diagrams show how the proposed bonuses are allocated, yet no failed withdrawal, false identity, or completed victim transaction appears in the evidence. At most, the offer is unverified.

citations.quote: There is a fee of 0.05 USD per visa.
from second direct referrals onward you can get bonus of 80% to all direct referrals under your account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanism is shown, not merely inferred: account activation requires a visa, entry and direct referrals are paired with 0.1 BTC amounts, and bonuses extend through referral levels. The conclusion explicitly tells viewers to ask partners for a referral link, says activation requires a donation, and promises guaranteed rewards. A scam classification does not require proving that a particular victim already paid or that the presenter personally controlled every transaction.
